scope: src/main.js lines 27050-29050 — reload (startReload/_startReloadP2), weapon switch, dropkick, wall-jump, slide, jump, vault, guard cover, EventBus, building clear, perk synergies + the large 'COMPREHENSIVE' data/function block (28200-29050).

findings.title: EventBus is instantiated and exposed but never emitted to or subscribed
findings.description: class EventBus is built, a singleton _eventBus is created, and it is exposed as window.__eventBus, but a repo-wide search shows _eventBus.emit / .on / .off and __eventBus.* are never called anywhere outside the class definition. The whole pub/sub layer is inert scaffolding.
findings.evidence: const _eventBus=new EventBus(); window.__eventBus=_eventBus;  // grep -nE "_eventBus\.(emit|on|off)|__eventBus\." returns nothing
findings.fix: Either delete EventBus + _eventBus + window.__eventBus (lines 28454-28463) as dead code, or actually wire it: e.g. call _eventBus.emit('kill',e) from the dropkick kill path and let HUD/audio subscribe. Lowest-risk: leave as a documented debug hook but mark it.
findings.risk: Removing it is safe (no callers). If kept, no behavior change. Don't break: it is harmless to leave.

findings.title: emitEvent() and EVENT_HOOKS telemetry ring buffer are never populated
findings.description: emitEvent pushes into EVENT_HOOKS (capped at 200) and optionally into window.__game.events, but emitEvent is never called from anywhere. EVENT_HOOKS therefore stays permanently empty; the telemetry/debug hook is non-functional.
findings.evidence: function emitEvent(name,data){ const ev={name,...}; EVENT_HOOKS.push(ev); ... }  // grep shows only the definition references emitEvent.
findings.fix: Delete emitEvent + EVENT_HOOKS (28886-28893) or insert emitEvent calls at real game milestones (kill, building-clear, boss-phase). No runtime effect either way today.
findings.risk: Safe to remove; nothing reads EVENT_HOOKS.

findings.title: logBuildingClear()/BUILDING_CLEAR_LOG never called and never restored from save
findings.description: logBuildingClear is defined but never invoked (the real building-advance flow is advanceBuilding() at line 37053). It also writes PROGRESS._buildingClearLog and calls saveProgressFile(), but _buildingClearLog is never read back on load, so even if it were called the stats would be a write-only, non-persisted blob. This is a feature half-wired so it never triggers AND a state-desync (written-but-never-read).
findings.evidence: function logBuildingClear(bn){...PROGRESS._buildingClearLog=BUILDING_CLEAR_LOG;saveProgressFile();}  // grep: logBuildingClear appears only at its definition; _buildingClearLog is only ever written, never read.
findings.fix: If a per-building clear log is desired, call logBuildingClear(G.building) inside advanceBuilding() (37053) and hydrate BUILDING_CLEAR_LOG from PROGRESS._buildingClearLog at load time (merged against defaults to preserve save compat). Otherwise delete 28482-28494.
findings.risk: Wiring it adds a saveProgressFile() write per building clear; keep the merge-against-defaults rule for clearance_progress. Deleting is fully safe.

findings.title: _applyMusicIntensityBoost writes MUSIC.intensity directly, contradicting the per-frame intensity lerp
findings.description: _applyMusicIntensityBoost sets MUSIC.intensity=min(1, MUSIC.intensity+boost) directly. The live music driver (lines 13238-13241) every frame does MUSIC.intensityTarget=want; MUSIC.intensity += (intensityTarget-intensity)*lerp. So any direct boost to MUSIC.intensity would be immediately pulled back toward intensityTarget on the next frame — the two writers disagree about who owns MUSIC.intensity. The function is currently never called (dead), so it's a latent contradiction rather than an active bug.
findings.fix: If music stingers are wanted, have _applyMusicIntensityBoost bump MUSIC.intensityTarget (and/or a transient floor) instead of MUSIC.intensity, so it survives the lerp. Otherwise delete the function + MUSIC_INTENSITY_BOOSTS table (29037-29051).
findings.risk: Low. As long as it stays uncalled there is no behavior change; if wired, target the same field the frame loop reads (intensityTarget).

findings.title: RECOIL_PATTERNS is a dead duplicate of the live RECOIL_PATTERNS_LEARNABLE table
findings.description: RECOIL_PATTERNS (per-weapon up/horiz/recovery/bloom) is defined but never read; the actual recoil system uses RECOIL_PATTERNS_LEARNABLE (defined at 25662, consumed at 25907) and RECOIL_STATE. Two recoil-pattern tables coexist with different values; the second one is inert. Risk: a future edit could 'tune recoil' in the dead table and see no effect, or someone could wire the wrong one and silently change recoil for every weapon.
findings.evidence: 28917: const RECOIL_PATTERNS={0:{up:.04,horiz:.015,...}, ...};  // grep -nE "RECOIL_PATTERNS\\b" (excluding _LEARNABLE) finds only this definition. Live system: 25662 RECOIL_PATTERNS_LEARNABLE, used at 25907.
findings.fix: Delete RECOIL_PATTERNS (28916-28925) to remove the ambiguity, or rename/merge into the learnable table if its values are the intended tuning. Do not wire it without reconciling values against RECOIL_PATTERNS_LEARNABLE.
findings.risk: Deleting is safe (no readers). Reconciling could change weapon recoil feel — verify against the live table first.

findings.title: MOVEMENT_FLAGS / _refreshMovementFlags are dead; canDodge/canDoubleJump never updated and never read
findings.description: MOVEMENT_FLAGS exposes canDodge/canDoubleJump initialized to false. _refreshMovementFlags() would set them from perks, but _refreshMovementFlags is never called, and MOVEMENT_FLAGS.canDodge/canDoubleJump are never read anywhere. Actual gating uses P._canDoubleJump (set at 31080 from hasPerk('doubleJump')) and hasPerk('dodgeRoll') (checked at 36734). So this is a fully redundant, never-refreshed shadow flag set — a contradiction-in-waiting (two sources of truth for the same capability).
findings.evidence: 28993-28994: MOVEMENT_FLAGS.canDodge=hasPerk('dodgeRoll'); MOVEMENT_FLAGS.canDoubleJump=hasPerk('doubleJump');  but grep for MOVEMENT_FLAGS.can* reads returns only these writes; _refreshMovementFlags has zero callers. Live gating: 27805 if(P._canDoubleJump...), 36734 if(!hasPerk('dodgeRoll'))return;
findings.fix: Delete MOVEMENT_FLAGS + _refreshMovementFlags (28982-28995), or make them the single source of truth and route the live checks through them. Do not leave both.
findings.risk: Safe to delete; nothing reads the flags. Consolidating risks subtle gating changes — verify double-jump/dodge still gate correctly.

findings.title: Large block of 'COMPREHENSIVE' helper functions are defined but never called
findings.description: A contiguous 'comprehensive' block contains many functions that are defined once and never invoked anywhere: pickOperatorReflection (28480), _broadcastSquadBark (28496), _enemyAtCover (28503), _enemiesNearPosition (28509), _allEnemiesInZone (28518), generateRunMemoir (28821), _giveEnemyPersonality (28806), _hpLabel (28856), _weaponStatRadar (28946), _findActiveSynergies (28938), _shouldBark (29029), compileFullRunStats (29053), _formatStatsForDisplay (29092). All show exactly one occurrence (their own definition). This is the bulk of the new uncommitted scaffolding; it inflates the file and creates many landmines (e.g. _giveEnemyPersonality mutates e.speed/idealDist/_sit/shootTimer/burstMax and would change AI tuning if ever wired).
findings.evidence: grep -c per symbol: pickOperatorReflection 2 (def+OPERATOR_REFLECTIONS list ref), _findActiveSynergies 1, _weaponStatRadar 1, generateRunMemoir 1, _giveEnemyPersonality 1, _hpLabel 1, _broadcastSquadBark 1, _enemyAtCover 1, _enemiesNearPosition 1, _allEnemiesInZone 1, _shouldBark 1, compileFullRunStats 1, _formatStatsForDisplay 1 — i.e. definition only.
findings.fix: Treat the whole 28480-29092 region as a quarantine: confirm with grep (done) and either remove the unused functions or wire the few that are intended (e.g. show generateRunMemoir on the run-end screen, call _findActiveSynergies in the loadout/pause UI). Keep the data tables that ARE used (ENEMY_POSE_STATES at 8392/8398 is live, RECOIL_PATTERNS_LEARNABLE is live — do NOT delete those).
findings.risk: Deleting genuinely-unreferenced functions is safe and shrinks main.js. Be careful NOT to delete ENEMY_POSE_STATES (used at 8392) or anything actually referenced; verify each symbol with grep before removal.

findings.title: _weaponStatRadar divides by w.spread and w.reloadTime with no zero-guard (latent NaN/Infinity)
findings.description: _weaponStatRadar computes range:Math.min(1,(.10/w.spread)/3) and accuracy:Math.min(1,1-w.spread*30) and handling:Math.min(1,(.5/w.reloadTime)). If any weapon has spread===0 (e.g. a future hitscan/precision weapon) range becomes Infinity and Math.min clamps it to 1, but if reloadTime===0 handling is Infinity->clamped, and accuracy can go negative. It is dead today (never called), so no current crash, but it would emit out-of-range/NaN radar values the moment it is wired to the loadout radar UI.
findings.fix: When wiring the radar, guard the divisors: use Math.min(1,(.10/Math.max(w.spread,1e-4))/3), clamp accuracy with Math.max(0,...), and Math.max(w.reloadTime,1e-3) for handling. Until then it is inert.
findings.risk: None while uncalled. If wired, missing guards produce malformed radar charts (clamped to 1 or negative).

findings.title: _spawnDropkickImpactFx creates a base slashMat that is cloned per slash but never used or disposed
findings.description: slashMat is created with new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial(...) at 27498, then slashMat.clone() is used for each of the 3 slash planes. The cloned materials are tracked in G.trails (mat:slash.material) and get disposed by _disposeTrail, but the ORIGINAL slashMat is never assigned to a mesh nor pushed to G.trails, so it is an orphaned material allocated on every dropkick-impact spawn and never disposed. Same pattern in _spawnSlideSkidFx (base mat at 27723, mat.clone() per puff) and _spawnDropkickLandingFx (dustMat at 27553, dustMat.clone() per puff). These are GPU material leaks proportional to dropkick/slide frequency.
findings.evidence: 27498: const slashMat=new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({...}); 27500: const slash=new THREE.Mesh(...,slashMat.clone()); // slashMat itself never added/disposed. _disposeTrail only frees the per-trail t.mat.
findings.fix: Either dispose the base after cloning (slashMat.dispose(); at the end of the slash loop / after the puff loop in each function), or build the material inline per element instead of clone(), or reuse a single cached module-level material. Lowest risk: add slashMat.dispose() after the for-loop in _spawnDropkickImpactFx (27509), dustMat.dispose() after the loop in _spawnDropkickLandingFx (27562), and mat.dispose() after the loop in _spawnSlideSkidFx (27736).
findings.risk: Low. Disposing the base material is safe because each mesh uses an independent clone(); the base is not referenced by any live object. Verify no later code reads slashMat/dustMat/mat after the loop (it does not).

findings.title: Dropkick launch has shake + gun dip but no camera FOV punch — cheap way to make the lunge read as a committed AAA move
findings.description: _startDropkick applies shakeY/shakeX and a small gunGrp dip, but does not punch FOV. A brief FOV widen on launch (then ease back) is the single cheapest cue that makes a flying-kick lunge feel powerful (Sifu/Doom-style). The codebase already animates camera params per-frame, so a transient _dropkickLaunchSurge is already set (27442) and could drive an FOV add.
findings.evidence: 27451-27454: PP.shakeY-=...; PP.shakeX+=...; gunGrp.position.y-=.038; gunGrp.position.z+=.042;  — no FOV/exposure punch. _dropkickLaunchSurge is set (27442) but only feeds body motion.
findings.fix: On launch set a transient fov-kick pulse (e.g. P._fovKick=Math.max(P._fovKick||0, P.dropkickTargeted?6:4)) and decay it in the camera update where FOV is composed; on contact (_checkDropkickHit, 27659) add a sharper inward FOV snap. Verify the project's existing FOV-composition site before adding a new field (search for camera.fov assignment).
findings.risk: Low-medium. Must hook into the existing FOV composition rather than writing camera.fov directly, or it will fight ADS/sprint FOV. Confirm the single FOV writer first.

findings.title: _hpLabel returns 'unknown' for ratio exactly 0 (dying band is half-open and excludes 0)
findings.description: HP_LABELS.dying is [.15,.0] and the loop matches with ratio<=range[0] && ratio>range[1] i.e. ratio>0. So a fully-drained enemy (ratio===0) does NOT match 'dying' and falls through to 'unknown'. Minor and currently dead (_hpLabel has no callers), but it is an off-by-edge in a state-label helper that would mislabel a dead/at-zero enemy if wired into AI transitions.
findings.evidence: 28859: if(ratio<=range[0]&&ratio>range[1])return k;  with dying:[.15,.0] -> ratio>0 required, so ratio===0 returns 'unknown' (28861).
findings.fix: Make the lowest band inclusive of zero: special-case the final band with ratio>=range[1], or change the loop to ratio<=range[0] && (ratio>range[1] || range[1]===0 && ratio>=0). Inert until _hpLabel is called.
findings.risk: None while uncalled. If wired, the fix prevents a misclassified 'unknown' AI state at 0 HP.
